raw_response:
I have farmed 30 years, so I do not start from zero. I start from what worked on my land and then I adjust a little. On 7 mu, money is still tight because if I spend more on fertilizer, then I have less left for spray, diesel, and hired help when work piles up. I have well water, so I will keep maize on the steadier land because water helps it hold yield, and I will keep some cotton because I know how to manage it and I do not want all my income sitting in one crop. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because the better ones usually fill grain better and stand better, and many people around here use hybrid now. I will feed maize a bit heavier on nitrogen because if maize goes hungry early, yield drops fast. For cotton, I will not be stingy with potash because cotton without enough strength drops squares and bolls too easily. I will plough once before planting because my ground sets a little hard after winter, then manage with rotary work where needed. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than watch yield fall, but I still keep it within what 7 mu can carry.
